question: A sum of ₹9,000 is lent partly at 7% and the remaining at 9% per annum. If the yearly interest on the average is 8.5%, then the sum (in ₹) which is lent at 9% is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of sums using Alligation = (Higher Rate − Avg Rate) : (Avg Rate − Lower Rate)

Ratio (7% : 9%) = (9 − 8.5) : (8.5 − 7) = 0.5 : 1.5 = 1 : 3

Total 4 units (1 + 3) = ₹9,000

Sum lent at 9% (3 units) = (9000 ÷ 4) × 3 = 2250 × 3 = ₹6,750

**∴ The correct answer is 6750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total principal = ₹9,000

Rate 1 = 7% | Rate 2 = 9%

Average interest rate = 8.5%

**Formula Used:**

Alligation Method: Ratio of quantities = (Rate₂ − Rateₐvg) : (Rateₐvg − Rate₁)

 Part 1 (7%) Part 2 (9%) Avg (8.5%) 
• 
• 
• 
• (9 − 8.5) = 0.5 (8.5 − 7) = 1.5 Ratio = 1 : 3 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio of sum lent at 7% to sum lent at 9% = (9 − 8.5) : (8.5 − 7)

⇒ Ratio = 0.5 : 1.5

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 3

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 1 + 3 = 4 units

⇒ 4 units = ₹9,000

⇒ 1 unit = 9000 ÷ 4 = ₹2,250

⇒ Sum lent at 9% = 3 units = 3 × 2,250

⇒ Sum lent at 9% = ₹6,750

**∴ The correct answer is 6750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It is a rule that enables us to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at their respective prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a specified price. Ratio = (Higher Rate − Mean Rate) / (Mean Rate − Lower Rate).

Weighted Average Interest Rate

If principal P₁ is lent at rate R₁ and P₂ at R₂, the average rate Rₐvg = (P₁R₁ + P₂R₂) ÷ (P₁ + P₂).

Simple Interest (SI)

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100. For one year (T=1), SI = (P × R) ÷ 100, which is simply the interest rate percentage applied to the principal.
